card.name: Kabasaran
card.era: Pre-colonial Minahasan warrior tradition; refined in the colonial era
card.tagline: Minahasan warrior dance of fierce red-clad fighters
card.profile: Kabasaran is a traditional Minahasan martial art and war dance from North Sulawesi, performed by men clad in red costumes wielding a sword (santi) with a shield, or a spear (wengkouw) (Wikipedia). The dancers, called kawasalan ('imitating fighting cocks'), are drawn from the hereditary Waranei (warrior) lineage. The word derives from kawasalan, related to the Moluccan Sakalele/Cakalele dance, which was simplified and combined with quadrille moves to create a dance suitable for welcoming Dutch guests. The basic structure uses nine sword or spear movements; dancers wear feathered headdresses and red woven cloth, with fierce wide-eyed expressions.
card.insight: Historians describe Kabasaran as a refinement of the rougher cakalele, deliberately softened with European quadrille movements to make it acceptable as a colonial welcoming dance (Hello Indonesia, citing Sutisno Kutoyo).
